set.approach: Leave the car in the Lake George lot, at the end of the Lakes Basin road above Mammoth, and follow the Crystal Lake trail. At the signed spur for Crystal Lake, turn left and drop down to the shore. Go a short way around the lake, then take the climbers trail that branches left and climbs to the foot of Crystal Crag. This northeast-facing wall is the first cliff you meet on the way to the Crag, and it can be seen from the parking lot.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Take Keller Peak Road above Running Springs; parking is limited along it, so pull completely off the pavement. The Lower Dinosaur Rock corridor is entered from the east: work around the foot of the north face of Lower Dinosaur Rock to reach the start of the corridor. Some scrambling is needed to reach the climbs, which line both walls of the narrow corridor.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Park by the gate at the end of West Pioneer Lane, off North Shore Drive; space is limited. Walk through the gate and head up the steep, rocky hillside past The Gardens boulders, splitting left or right to reach the formation you want.

set.approach: Park at Lake George and walk around the right-hand side of the lake. Climb the dry creek bed, or the trail on the north side of it, until a huge boulder in the creek comes into view; the wall is just above that boulder. The wall faces north above Crystal Creek and is best visited when the creek is low. A second way in is the Crystal Lake trail, turning left at the lake and descending to the wall.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Drive to the end of the road at Horseshoe Lake, where there is a very large parking area, and take the Mammoth Pass trail to McLeod Lake. Walk around the right-hand shore, counterclockwise, to the southwest side. Enter the trees there and look for a well-worn path, then a smaller trail that climbs the hillside toward the rocks. Once you find it, the trail is well marked all the way to the wall.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Reach the end of the Cherry Hill Road system near Taylor Meadow, where a dirt road ends at the trailhead. High-clearance vehicles can go a little farther up a logging road to within sight of the domes; others park at the road's end and walk in. The hike follows a well-cairned route, and expect the access road to close with the first heavy snowfall of winter.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: From the northern parking area at the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, walk east past the Incinerator Wall; the long, slender formation comes into view and the trail is well defined. From the Amphitheatre area (Claim Jumper, Gunsmoke and Thunderbird walls), several trails lead northeast to it. The east face is the shorter, slabby side.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Follow the Cathedral Lakes trail, which is part of the John Muir Trail, to the point where the toe of the North Buttress comes close to the path. The toe is only a short step off the trail. The newer routes lie on the west and north sides of the buttress near its toe.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.

set.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and hike around the left-hand side of the lake to its far shore. From there a climbers trail leads up the hillside to the cliff. This is the long north side of Dike Wall, shaded for most of the day; a large snowbank can sit under it and make climbing here difficult until late in the season.

set.approach: Start from the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends, and follow the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall sits right beside the trail and is the first of the Brownstone walls you reach. The crag is shaded from morning until mid-afternoon, and the trail itself is sunny, so an early start is wise.

set.approach: From Fawnskin, take Rim of the World Drive north, then forest road 2N13 west on graded dirt, and turn right onto 2N68. A hairpin turn on 2N68 holds a small parking area with room for only a handful of cars. The trail starts north from the apex of the hairpin, crests a small rise, drops across a seasonal stream, and switchbacks up to the Dragonlance Wall, where the formations begin.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no descent source.
